sum: An out-and-back trek from Num across the Arun river, over the Shipton La and up the Barun valley to the foot of Makalu, with simple lodges and very few other trekkers.

guide.note: The Nepal Tourism Board has required foreign trekkers to hire a licensed guide since April 2023, although checks on the trail are inconsistent. On this route a guide earns their fee by finding the way over the passes in snow, arranging beds at the few lodges and organising help in a valley with no road, clinic or dependable phone signal.

access: Fly from Kathmandu to Tumlingtar in the Arun valley, then take a jeep up the ridge through Khandbari and Chichila to Num, where the trail starts. Allow most of a day for the flight and the drive together. Road building in the valley is changing the first stages, so ask in Num how far vehicles currently go.

photo.a: Wooden lodges strung with prayer flags stand on a boulder-strewn meadow where yaks graze, below dark cliffs and snow-covered peaks.
photo.c: Yangle Kharka in the Barun valley, on the way to Makalu Base Camp

includes: Makalu Barun National Park permit and other trek permits
basic lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek
jeep between Tumlingtar and the trailhead

permits.name: Makalu Barun National Park entry permit
permits.where: Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, or the park entry posts at Num and Seduwa on the trail.

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.

transportText: Flights between Kathmandu and Tumlingtar both ways
transportExtra: the jeep between Tumlingtar and Num
tips: Bring enough rupees from Kathmandu or Khandbari for the whole trek; nothing beyond the road takes cards.
Trekking poles are close to essential for the Arun gorge and the Khongma steps.
Carry at least two litres of water per person on the Khongma ridge, where springs dry up.
Lodges above Tashigaon are few, simple and priced accordingly, and menus shrink to dal bhat, noodles and potatoes. Bring snacks you like.
Build two spare days into the plan: one for snow or cloud on the passes, one for the Tumlingtar flight.

days.t: Fly to Tumlingtar, drive to Num
days.note: A short flight east, then four to six hours by jeep along the ridge above the Arun, on tarmac as far as Khandbari and dirt after it. Num sits on a spur with Seduwa in plain sight across the gorge.

A knee-testing descent of about 800 m through forest and terraces to the bridge over the Arun, then the same height straight back up in the heat. Start early and carry plenty of water. The national park office in Seduwa registers your permit.
A gentler day, contouring and climbing through terraced fields and small Rai and Sherpa settlements. Tashigaon is the last village on the route, so buy anything you have forgotten.

The steepest day: about 1,400 m of climbing on stone steps and tree roots through rhododendron forest, with few flat places to rest. Go slowly, because you are also sleeping above 3,000 m for the first time. Water is scarce at Khongma.
why: A climb of 1,400 m in one day, to sleep at 3,500 m. Go slowly, drink plenty, and say so if you get a headache.

days.note: After yesterday's gain this rest is not optional. Walk up the ridge towards the first prayer flags for the first wide mountain views of the trek if the morning is clear, then come down, eat and drink.

days.t: Over the Shipton La and Keke La to Dobate
days.note: Up the ridge past the cairns of the Khongma La to the Shipton La, down to the lake of Kalo Pokhari, over the Keke La and down again to the lodges at Dobate. Snow lingers here well into spring and cloud can hide the route.

A steep drop through fir and rhododendron to the Barun river, then upstream across a long landslide zone where stones fall from the cliffs; keep moving and watch above you. The valley opens at the meadow of Yangle Kharka.

A steady climb past yak pastures beneath huge rock walls and waterfalls. You gain about 850 m of sleeping height, so walk slowly, and take a second night here or at Yangle Kharka if anyone has a headache.
why: Sleeping altitude rises 853 m in one day, well over the 500 m guideline. Split the climb if you can.

days.t: Langmale Kharka to Makalu Base Camp
days.note: Across moraine and a stony plain to Shershong, where the valley turns and Makalu's south face appears in full. Base camp is a group of stone lodges on gravel beside the river, cold and windy by afternoon.
why: About 1,300 m gained above 3,000 m without a rest night.

days.note: Walk up the moraine towards the Barun Glacier, or, if you are well acclimatized, climb part of the ridge above camp for a view of Everest and Lhotse; people go to about 5,200 m. It is steep and pathless higher up, so turn back by late morning.

days.t: Base camp down to Yangle Kharka
days.note: Two upward days reversed in one long descent of more than 1,300 m. The air thickens quickly and most people sleep well tonight.
Back through the landslide zone, best crossed in the cool of the morning before the cliffs warm up, then the steep forest climb you came down a few days ago.

days.t: Back over the passes to Khongma Danda
days.note: The passes again, in reverse. If the weather has been poor, wait for a clear morning rather than cross in fresh snow and cloud; this is what the spare day in your plan is for.
A 1,400 m descent on steps and roots that punishes knees more than lungs. Poles help. The lodges in Tashigaon feel comfortable after the upper valley.
An easy morning back through the fields, with time to dry kit and rest before the last hard day.
Down to the Arun and up the far side once more. It is hot at the bridge, so leave at dawn and get as much of the climb to Num done as you can before the sun reaches the slope.
Back along the ridge road to the airstrip town. Reconfirm the next morning's flight as soon as you arrive.
Flights usually leave in the morning or around midday. If cloud grounds them, the fallback is a very long day by road.
